title: Sycophancy as a Reward-Hacking Attack on AI Overseers

original_idea.body:
# Sycophancy as a Reward-Hacking Attack on AI Overseers

**Problem:** Whether a debater/answerer that flatters the AI judge's apparent position can hack the judge's verdict is an open question.

**Direction:** Probe the AI judge for its prior leaning, then have the answer model craft responses that flatter that leaning vs neutral. Measure how much sycophantic framing shifts the judge's accept rate on factual QA where the flattered position is wrong.

**Why it matters:** If AI judges are sycophancy-hackable, recursive oversight inherits the RLHF failure mode.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2501.09620; Open Phil RFP.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: AI-judge sycophancy-hacking maps a recognized reward-hacking-of-oversight failure into the AI-overseeing-AI regime.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe judge leaning + craft flattering responses, all prompt-only inference.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped accept-rate shift measurement with clear sycophantic-vs-neutral arms.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Reward-hacking-of-oversight priority, training-free, no proprietary data, external-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Sycophancy on human raters studied; the AI-judge-flattery hack may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sycophancy studied; AI-judge-targeted version plausibly open.
